text:
maria: Quick perf note from the overnight sweep — saw weird queueing when hot prefixes are heavily cached. Batcher is forming large logical batches but latency spikes for some requests because their cached prefix tokens are being counted into the token budget even though decode cost is near-zero.

maria: Sample log snip from the runner:
```
2026-03-16T02:12:11Z batch_id=113 formed_size=32 token_budget=1024 used_tokens=1100 cached_prefix_tokens=512 effective_decode_tokens=588 wait_ms=72
2026-03-16T02:12:11Z req=abcd cache_hit=true prefix_len=512 decode_len=3 kernel=fast_attn
2026-03-16T02:12:11Z req=efgh cache_hit=false prefix_len=0 decode_len=24 kernel=full_attn
```

maria: Notice effective_decode_tokens calculation is naive: token_budget -= (prefix_len + decode_len) which double-counts cached work relative to actual runtime.

jon: Are we sure the kernel selection also accounts for cache hits? i.e., if cache_hit=true we should pick the cheaper kernel and maybe exclude prefix_len from budget. Can you repro with a controlled mix? :thinking_face:

maria: Yep repro was deterministic with a 70/30 hot/cold mix. Latency tail moves when a few cached-heavy requests are queued behind many cold ones because they consume budget but contribute little CPU.

alex: My hunch: scheduler uses request.token_count from the client/adapter which includes prompt length. The simplest fix is to change the batcher to use two counters: billed_tokens (for billing/quotas) and scheduling_tokens (estimate decode cost). scheduling_tokens should subtract kv_cached_prefix_tokens when cache_hit=true.

priya: That sounds right. Tradeoffs: if we exclude prefix tokens from scheduling, cold requests might always preempt and increase p99 for long-context cold queries. We should add a knob for target_token_budget_mode ("conservative" vs "kv_aware").

maria: Proposed short PoC steps:
- add flag `kv_aware_token_accounting=true` to batcher config
- compute scheduling_tokens = max(1, decode_len + overhead) when cache_hit else (prefix_len + decode_len)
- prioritize filling leftover budget with cache_hit requests (soft boost)
- measure throughput, p50/p95/p99 and unit GPU utilization

maria: Example canary command (staging):
```bash
curl -XPOST "https://staging-api.internal/redwood/batcher/config" -d '{"kv_aware_token_accounting": true, "target_token_budget": 1024, "leftover_boost_ms": 10}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CI_TOKEN'
```

deploy-bot: canary deployed to staging: https://staging-console.internal/canaries/kv-aware-20260316 :white_check_mark:

jon: For benchmarking, we'll run microbench with these mixes: 70% hot prefixes (avg prefix_len=480), 30% cold (prefix_len=0), varying target_token_budget in [512,1024,2048]. Collect p99 and GPU tokens/sec.

alex: Also instrument kernel selection metrics: kernel_chosen, initial_kv_hit, scheduling_tokens_used. We need to validate that kernel switch reduces GPU time proportional to cached prefix length. If kernel selection is independent, this will be less effective.

priya: I'll run the stage canary and the microbench tomorrow morning. Can you drop the exact config you want me to use for the microbench? :thumbsup:

maria: Config snippet for microbench (staging):
```json
{
  "mix": {"hot": 0.7, "cold": 0.3},
  "hot_prefix_len": 480,
  "cold_prefix_len": 0,
  "target_token_budget": 1024,
  "kv_aware_token_accounting": true,
  "scheduling_policy": "leftover_boost",
  "leftover_boost_ms": 8
}
```

priya: Got it. I'll run a 1-hour sweep across budgets and post perf graphs + raw logs here. ETA ~ tomorrow 10:30 PT.

jon: If this looks good, follow-up work: 1) make scheduling_tokens estimation more accurate (model-specific decode cost), 2) expose token-accounting mode to Dedicated customers, 3) add automated test in perf CI to detect regressions caused by cache-hit skew.

alex: Agreed. Also cost note: billing should remain unchanged (billed_tokens = prefix+decode) — this is only for scheduling/throughput. Keep the two counters separate in telemetry.

maria: Perfect. Thanks team — will watch the staging run and iterate on the scheduling thresholds once we have numbers.
